name: Filippo Carafa della Serra
summary:
Filippo Carafa della Serra was an Italian Cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church.

Born in Naples, Italy around 1340, Filippo Carafa della Serra rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become a cardinal by 1378. He played a significant role in the papal conclave that elected Pope Gregory XI, who in turn reinstated the French monarchy's influence over Italy.

Carafa della Serra's influence extended beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he was also involved in Italian politics and supported the rule of King Robert of Naples. His connections to powerful families like the Caraffas and the Sanseverinos helped shape the complex web of alliances that defined medieval Italy.

Despite his importance within the Catholic Church, Filippo Carafa della Serra's legacy is largely overshadowed by more prominent figures of the time. Nevertheless, his contributions to Italian politics and ecclesiastical affairs demonstrate a lasting impact on the region.

The imposing frescoes in the Palatine Chapel at the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta in Cremona, Italy, bear witness to Filippo Carafa della Serra's enduring artistic legacy.
